title: Evolutionary repurposing of a pore-forming toxin drives epithelial remodeling during terrestrial adaptation
title_zh: 孔形成性毒素的进化性再利用驱动陆生适应过程中的上皮重塑
abstract: The ability of vertebrates to conquer land is attributed to innovations in respiration and locomotion. However, land adaptation profoundly reshaped mucosal surfaces such as the skin, the main interface between hosts and the environment. To adapt to land, African lungfish annually remodel their skin, forming a cocoon. Here, we report the discovery of a small pore-forming toxin in African lungfish, Protop-CrTX-A, with no other vertebrate counterpart that is sufficient to drive epithelial morphogenesis transcriptional programs. In free-swimming lungfish, goblet cells secrete Protop-CrTX-A into the mucus. During estivation, this niche is replaced by a mucin-low/basal epithelial niche, adjacent to a granulocyte immune niche that becomes the predominant source of Protop-CrTX-A in the estivated skin. Protop-CrTX-A acts as a reversible switch for skin remodeling, sufficient to convert African lungfish skin between aquatic and terrestrial states. We propose that innate immunity, through its capacity to remodel tissues, was a key driver of vertebrate water-land transitions.
abstract_zh: 脊椎动物征服陆地的能力被归因于呼吸和运动方面的创新。然而，陆地适应深刻重塑了黏膜表面，如皮肤，皮肤是宿主与环境之间的主要界面。为了适应陆地，非洲肺鱼每年重塑其皮肤，形成茧。在此，我们报道了在非洲肺鱼中发现一种小型孔形成性毒素Protop-CrTX-A，在其他脊椎动物中没有对应物，足以驱动上皮形态发生转录程序。在自由游动的肺鱼中，杯状细胞将Protop-CrTX-A分泌至黏液中。在休眠期间，这一生态位被黏蛋白低/基底上皮生态位取代，该生态位邻近成为卧泡皮肤中Protop-CrTX-A主要来源的粒细胞免疫生态位。Protop-CrTX-A作为皮肤重塑的可逆开关，足以将非洲肺鱼皮肤在水生与陆生状态之间转换。我们提出，先天免疫通过其重塑组织的能力，是脊椎动物水-陆过渡的关键驱动因素。
